verses.text: But teach what fits sound doctrine.
Teach older men to be clear-minded, dignified, and self-controlled, sound in faith, love, and endurance.
In the same way, teach older women to live reverently, not slander others or be controlled by too much wine. They should teach what is good,
so they can train younger women to love their husbands and children,
to be sensible and pure, care for their households, be kind, and submit to their husbands, so God's word won't be slandered.
In the same way, encourage younger men to be self-controlled.
In everything, show yourself as an example of good works. In your teaching, show integrity, dignity,
and sound speech that can't be condemned, so anyone who opposes you will have nothing bad to say about us.
Teach enslaved people to submit to their masters and try to please them in everything. They shouldn't talk back
or steal, but should show complete trustworthiness, so that in every way they make the teaching about God our Savior attractive.
God's grace has appeared, bringing salvation to all people.
It teaches us to reject godlessness and worldly desires, and to live with self-control, righteousness, and devotion to God in this present age,
as we wait for the blessed hope—the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ.
He gave himself for us to set us free from all wickedness and to make us pure, his own people, eager to do what is good.
Teach these things. Encourage and correct with full authority. Don't let anyone disregard you.
